subject: research/chip-abc-order
professional: a senior logic-synthesis researcher / EDA engineer who has published on ABC and Yosys flows (structural bias, choice-based mapping, datapath synthesis); first checks: are the rewrites truly equivalence-preserving and proved so, is the effect real under an independent re-synthesis, is the metric honest (area vs depth), and is the mechanism and prior work on structural bias acknowledged

evidence.correctness: Installed Yosys 0.33 (git sha1 2584903a060, same as results.txt). experiments/run.py in a scratch copy (/tmp/claude-0/audit-chip-abc-order/copy, 3 min 58 s) regenerated results.txt byte-identically (diff empty). Independent recompute: a carry-select adder hand-written from scratch (/tmp/claude-0/audit-chip-abc-order/indep/mk.py, no subject import) with every block in order a+b+c, c+a+b, etc., synthesised with my own yosys command lines: order a+b+cin gives 95x22=2090 (default), 112x11=1232 (dch), 111x15=1665 (resyn2), matching the README's 'as generated' column; order cin+a+b gives 84x27=2268 (default, the README max) and 128x8=1024 (dch, the README min). Equivalence re-checked by a different method (Icarus Verilog, 300,000 random vectors plus corners vs a+b): 0 mismatches for two hand-written orders and for two subject-generated shuffle+rename+permute variants. Ratio 1750/1220=1.434 and 1-1024/1232=16.9% recomputed by hand. Numbers are right; the framing of the 1024 'win' is not (see claims).
evidence.completeness: Every reproduce step ran: unittest 4 tests OK in 1.7 s; run.py regenerates results.txt identically (about 4 min, README says about 6); figure.py's SVG labels (2090, 2268, 1024, 1408, 1220, 1750) match results.txt; live page https://marisstella.app/research/chip-abc-order/ returns 200 and carries the 1.43 figure. No stubs or TODOs. Next steps list two items that have since been done in research/chip-abc-orderpass and research/chip-abc-orderblocks without the README saying so.
evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 4 tests OK. Three mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, two survived: dropping `-verify` from the sat prover in flow.py:47 (confirmed by hand to make a deliberately non-equivalent adder 'prove' equivalent: rc 0 instead of 1) and breaking the depth regex in flow.py:39 (depth silently becomes 0, cells x depth becomes 0). Only disabling the operand shuffle in variants.py:35 was caught. There is no negative test for the equivalence checker, so the README's '0 failures of 288' guarantee is unguarded, and nothing tests a score value.
evidence.craft: Read flow.py, variants.py, gens.py, run.py, figure.py, tests/test_variants.py. Small and readable. Defects: flow.score returns cells=0/depth=0 when its regexes do not match instead of raising (flow.py:38-40, a silent fallback that would score a variant as a perfect 0); Verilog is rewritten by regex (variants.py:5,37), acceptable for the generator's narrow output but undocumented as such; tests open files without closing (ResourceWarning); the figure's 'over 12 operand orders' range also includes the base text (run.py:281).
evidence.claims: Numbers in the README table and bullets are all backed by results.txt and reproduced. Unbacked or misleading: (1) title and intro say the texts 'differ only cosmetically', but reordering a left-associative `a + b + c` chain changes the expression tree ((a+b)+c vs (c+a)+b), which is what lets opt_merge share a+b (the follow-up chip-abc-orderpass found exactly this); (2) 'best variant under dch_map (1024) beats ... the best adder (1232) by 17%' omits that it has 128 cells vs 112 (+14% area) and wins only on depth 8 vs 11; (3) Limitations says shuffle is a no-op on csel4, but 12 of 12 csel4 shuffle variants differ in text (the output-slice assigns are reordered); (4) suspected alumacc/macc mechanism and Next steps are stale after chip-abc-orderpass. Limits, AI-assistance note and tool version are stated.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on it, and two did (chip-abc-orderpass, chip-abc-orderblocks). Nearest prior work: structural bias in ABC mapping (Chatterjee, Mishchenko, Brayton et al., 'Reducing structural bias in technology mapping', ICCAD 2005 / IEEE TCAD 2006, the origin of the dch choice computation used here) and datapath rewriting that removes sensitivity to written expression structure (Coward, Constantinides, Drane, e-graph datapath optimisation, ARITH 2022); neither is cited. The result (QoR depends on how a sum is parenthesised, via sharing) is sound but known in kind; its value is as an internal caveat for the repo's proposer loops, one structure, 12 samples of a 6^7 order space.
evidence.domain: A synthesis researcher would accept the miter+SAT equivalence step and the pinned tool version, but would flag: cells x depth on a generic-gate library is a proxy that here hides an area-for-depth trade; 'cosmetic' conflates text with expression structure; sampling 12 of 6^7 orders when the whole space per block-type (6 orders, verified uniform here in 18 runs) is cheap to enumerate; no explanation of mechanism (the cause is resource sharing by opt_merge, a front-end effect, not ABC).

Mechanism guess (alumacc/macc) and Next steps are stale: chip-abc-orderpass found opt_merge sharing, chip-abc-orderblocks ran the enumeration; README not updated or linked

verdict: The numbers are right: the full experiment regenerates byte-identically on Yosys 0.33, and an independently hand-written carry-select adder reproduces 2090/1232/1665 as generated and the 2268 and 1024 extremes after reordering, with variant equivalence confirmed by 300,000-vector Icarus simulation. It does not meet the bar: verification is weak (the SAT prover and the depth parser can be broken with all four tests green), the README frames an expression-tree change as cosmetic and a depth-for-area trade (+14% cells) as a 17% win, and it does not cite the structural-bias literature that predicts the effect. Sound as an internal caveat for the repo's proposer loops, and two follow-ups built on it; not new in kind.
